Concordance of trends across sources

Source: R/trend_index.R
trend_concordance.Rd

Measures whether sources move together: the weighted share of sources whose trend change over a lag has the sign of the weighted majority, and the share of variance of the first principal component of source trend growth rates, each compared with a placebo distribution obtained by circular shifts of the source series.

Usage

trend_concordance(
  tr,
  source_col,
  time_col,
  lags = c(13L, 52L),
  weights = NULL,
  n_perm = 200L,
  seed = 1L,
  value_col = "trend"
)

Arguments

tr

A data.frame or data.table with one row per source x week (e.g. totals from extract_trend()).

source_col

Name of the source column.

time_col

Name of the time column (weekly Date or IDate).

lags

Integer vector of lags in weeks.

weights

NULL (equal weights) or a data.frame with columns source_col and w.

n_perm

Number of placebo shifts (non-negative integer).

seed

Seed of the placebo shifts; the global RNG state is restored.

value_col

Name of the trend column (default "trend").

Value

A data.table with one row per lag x statistic (concordance, pc1_share) and columns lag, statistic, observed, placebo_mean, placebo_q95, p_value and n_perm. Attribute by_time: columns time_col, lag, concordance and n_sources.

Details

For lag h (weeks), the growth of source s is g_{s,t} = trend_{s,t} - trend_{s,t-h}. In week t, with W+ and W- the weights of sources with positive and negative growth and W the weight of sources with non-missing growth, the concordance is max(W+, W-) / W (1 when all sources agree, 0.5 when split evenly); the statistic concordance is its mean over weeks with at least two sources. pc1_share is the share of variance of the first principal component of the standardised growth matrix (complete weeks only, unweighted). The placebo shifts the growth series of each source circularly by an independent random offset, which keeps the autocorrelation of each source and destroys the alignment across sources; p_value = (1 + #(placebo >= observed)) / (n_perm + 1).

Examples

weeks <- data.table::as.IDate("2024-01-01") + 7L * (0:79)
set.seed(2)
tr <- data.table::data.table(
  source = rep(c("a", "b", "c"), each = 80), week = rep(weeks, 3),
  trend = c(cumsum(rnorm(80)), cumsum(rnorm(80)), cumsum(rnorm(80)))
)
trend_concordance(tr, "source", "week", lags = 4L, n_perm = 50L)
#>      lag   statistic  observed placebo_mean placebo_q95   p_value n_perm
#>    <int>      <char>     <num>        <num>       <num>     <num>  <int>
#> 1:     4 concordance 0.7192982    0.7486842   0.7743421 0.9215686     50
#> 2:     4   pc1_share 0.4815653    0.4283812   0.4876650 0.1176471     50
